name: SCP Archive
description: An archive of original SCP Foundation articles.

entries.title: Noticed
entries.hook: Over forty-six years, the Foundation arrives at a question it had been institutionally resisting since 1971: why are all the anomalies on Earth?

entries.title: The Resolution
entries.hook: The universe has a bug. A quiet population of pattern-recognisers — hyperphantasic, autistic, attentive — has been perceiving it for centuries without knowing what they were noticing. The Foundation has decided not to tell them.

entries.title: The Short Way Home
entries.hook: A small B-road in England takes sixteen seconds longer to drive south than north. A network of 350+ such roads has been maintained across Europe for at least 4,400 years.

entries.title: The Larger Half
entries.hook: SCP-033's missing number was the first element of a much larger set. Human mathematics is a proper subset of mathematics. Every theorem ever proved is incomplete.

entries.title: Below the Noise
entries.hook: Tens of thousands of unconnected people are performing coordinated actions in unison, without any awareness of doing so. The targets align with a political pattern. The participants do not.

entries.title: How Far It Goes
entries.hook: A hobbyist researcher with an exceptionally effective AI-assisted toolkit spends seven years engineering memetic malware. He disappears. The Foundation watches the eighty-one researchers in the world with comparable toolkits.

entries.title: She Just Dreams
entries.hook: An amateur fiction writer publishes short horror stories online. 31% of them turn out to correspond exactly to real Foundation anomalies. She has no anomalous properties whatsoever. She is, by every available measure, perfectly ordinary.

entries.title: The Other Bench
entries.hook: A retired electrician carves an impossible shape from walnut after seeing it once in a dream. The dream featured someone else in the workshop, teaching by example. The student is finished. The teacher is still working.

entries.title: The Gift
entries.hook: A small London hamlet has a 40% lower rate of mental health problems than the regional average. The cause is a mycorrhizal fungus that gently prompts the brain's own mood-regulatory processes. The Foundation has decided to share it.

entries.title: Knocked
entries.hook: An independent researcher uses LLM-assisted optimisation to speed up a mathematical integral by a factor of a million. The physics forbids it. Something on the other side of the door has been waiting a long time to be found.

entries.title: Read-Heads
entries.hook: An IT security firm uses gravitational wave data as an entropy source. After three black hole events produce correlated 'random' numbers, the Foundation discovers the signal is the digits of π expressed in base 17.
